purpose: The crosswalk from the canonical Work Request lifecycle to the Workspace's user-facing projection. Doctrine names writing this as a Phase 1 Foundation deliverable and neither planning document contains it.

authority.canonical_doctrine: carr-control-room-bduf section 13.2 — 'This lifecycle is canonical across products; the Workspace request view is a mapped, non-authoritative safe projection (council ruling 2026-08-12).'
authority.projection_doctrine: carr-workspace-bduf section 10.1 — 'These user-facing states are a mapped, non-authoritative projection of the canonical Work Request lifecycle ... the server enforces the canonical machine (council ruling 2026-08-12).'
authority.who_publishes_this: The Control Room, because doctrine's product boundary gives it ownership of work requests. A projection does not get to define itself.

granted_projection_states.source: carr-workspace-bduf section 10.1 lists exactly these seven and no others.
granted_projection_states.THIS_IS_A_CLOSED_SET: The projection may render only these. A state absent here cannot be shown even if some contract file declares it — the canonical machine plus this crosswalk is the whole permitted surface.

crosswalk.note: Recorded, not yet triaged. The requester's view is the same in all three intake states: it is in the queue.
Triage is internal disposition and carries no requester-visible change.
Ready to claim is still waiting from the requester's side.
Verification is work. Nothing is finished until it is accepted.
Waiting on a release window is still not done.
The only canonical state that may render as completed.
A named human decision is outstanding.
Blocked carries blocker_code and blocker_detail by canonical invariant; the projection shows that something is needed and the reason field carries what.

invariants: TOTAL: every canonical state, main and side, maps to exactly one projection state. An unmapped canonical state is a contract defect, not a rendering choice.
CLOSED: every projection target appears in granted_projection_states. The crosswalk cannot introduce a state doctrine did not grant.
NOT INJECTIVE, ON PURPOSE: several canonical states share a projection target. Collapsing detail is what makes the projection safe; the canonical record keeps the distinction.
ONE WAY: this maps canonical to projection and never the reverse. A projection state does not determine a canonical state, so no UI action may set canonical state by choosing a label.

REASON SURVIVES COLLAPSE: wherever two canonical states share a target, the reason or blocker detail from the canonical record must accompany the projected state, or the collapse loses the only thing that distinguished them.

judgment_calls.decision: released projects to in_progress, not completed.
judgment_calls.why: The canonical machine's own invariant is that confirmed_closed requires accepted verification evidence. Released means shipped, not confirmed. Rendering completed at release would assert an outcome the record does not yet hold, and the requester would believe the work was done while verification could still fail or roll back.
judgment_calls.cost_accepted: A requester whose fix is live sees in_progress, which understates reality for the window between release and confirmation. Understating is the safe direction: the alternative claims a result that is not yet evidenced.
judgment_calls.reopens_if: A distinct released-but-unconfirmed projection state is ever granted to the Workspace view by doctrine, which would remove the need to collapse it.

judgment_calls.why: Doctrine grants the projection seven states and superseded is not among them, while superseded IS a canonical terminal. It must map somewhere. declined is the nearest granted terminal that does not falsely claim the work was done. The canonical reason field carries what actually happened, and the canonical machine already requires every side exit to record a reason.
judgment_calls.cost_accepted: declined reads as a rejection to a requester whose request was in fact absorbed into another one. The reason text has to carry that weight, and if it is thin the projection is misleading.
judgment_calls.reason_carrier: ops.work_request.exit_reason and superseded_by, surfaced together as the sourced card's withdrawal block (exit_reason, closed_at, superseded_by_ref). Named here because REASON SURVIVES COLLAPSE had no enforcement site until migration 0426 made these two terminals reachable: before it, superseded was declared by the canonical machine and entered by nothing, so the cost above was hypothetical. It is now paid on real rows, and the successor's human ref is what keeps 'absorbed into WR-n' from reading as 'rejected'.
judgment_calls.reopens_if: The reason field proves insufficient in practice, or doctrine grants the projection a superseded state. Either would be a better answer than this mapping.

known_conflict_this_contract_exposes.what: workspace/contracts/state-machines.v1.json#machines.engineering_request declares NINE states — it adds draft and superseded to doctrine's seven.
known_conflict_this_contract_exposes.why_it_matters: A projection cannot invent states its canonical source did not authorise. superseded is specifically a canonical side state doctrine did not extend to the view, and draft has no canonical counterpart at all: the canonical machine's initial state is captured.
known_conflict_this_contract_exposes.on_draft: draft is best understood as a pre-request composition state that exists only in the browser before a request is captured. It is not a Work Request state and should not appear in a machine that claims to project one.
known_conflict_this_contract_exposes.resolution: Trim the projection contract to the seven granted states. NOT done in this file, deliberately: this contract's job is to state the mapping, and editing the other product's contract is a separate change that should be reviewed on its own terms.

not_this_contract.approval_lifecycle: Doctrine defines a separate Approval object — Draft, Proposed, Revised, then Approved, Rejected or Expired, then Executing, then Verified, Failed or Rolled back — which gates production mutation OF a work request. It interlocks with this machine and is not part of it. Merging the two would be a design error.
not_this_contract.persistence: This crosswalk remains the mapping, not the storage. Work Requests are now persisted once in ops.work_request (migration 0114) inside the same canonical Neon store, with the ops schema providing the least-privilege namespace. Program ordering and session context for the fixed AI capability portfolio extend those same rows in migration 0125; no second request or queue source of truth exists.
not_this_contract.storage_boundary_settled: The apparent planning conflict is resolved by namespace rather than a second store: operational metadata lives in the distinct ops schema while Neon Postgres remains the single canonical record store. Business payloads and secrets do not belong on Work Request rows.
